Safety, password and time gates run before targeting. The first matching device rule wins; if none matches, the first matching country rule wins. Otherwise the link's main destination is used. An OS and device in the same rule must both match. Each device rule must specify at least one of them. Supported OS values are ios, android, windows, macos; devices are mobile, tablet, desktop. Device/OS comes from the request user agent and country from the trusted Cloudflare CF-IPCountry header. Country rules use uppercase two-letter codes. Unknown OS/country values do not match those predicates.

Every target URL must pass public HTTP(S) structural validation. All configured targets are included in safety scans, even when they are not selected for the current visitor. Editing the destination set queues a new scan and supersedes older scans. Query forwarding, fixed UTM and permanent redirect behavior apply to the selected destination.

Weighted rotation

A rotation list selects among one to ten public HTTP(S) destinations after all gates and device/country rules:

{
  "rules": {
    "rotation": [
      { "url": "https://example.com/a", "weight": 1 },
      { "url": "https://example.com/b", "weight": 3 }
    ]
  }
}

Weights are relative: this example assigns about one quarter of fresh selections to A and three quarters to B. Each weight must be positive, finite and no greater than 1,000,000. All rotation URLs are structurally validated and included in safety scans. Changing only weights does not require rescanning the same destinations.

The first selection sets a host-only _sr_{linkId} cookie for one hour, with Secure, HttpOnly and SameSite=Lax. It stores a configuration fingerprint and option number rather than a visitor identifier. Subsequent visits reuse that option without refreshing expiry. Changing URLs, option order or weights invalidates the previous fingerprint and selects again. Malformed or out-of-range cookie values are ignored. Without cookies, each request gets a fresh selection.

Device/country matches and safety/password/time gates do not create a rotation cookie. Query forwarding, fixed UTM and permanent redirect settings apply to the selected option. Use the default 302 when rotation changes should reach returning visitors promptly; clients may remember permanent redirects.

Branch analytics

Targeted destination clicks carry m.branch: device:0, geo:0, rotation:0, and so on, or destination when no targeting rule matched. Numbers are zero-based rule positions; editing or reordering rules changes what a position represents. Links without targeting retain the existing event format, with no branch field.

The REST analytics endpoints accept groupBy=branch and branch=geo:0 filters, subject to the existing analytics-breakdown plan gate and workspace isolation. The click pipeline preserves branch values during retries, and daily rollups include byBranch. Safety/password/time gates produce no destination click. The dashboard branch breakdown view remains part of the advanced management UI work; the REST breakdown is available now.

Permanent redirects

permanent: true uses HTTP 301 for the final destination hop. The default remains HTTP 302. Destination clicks are still enqueued, and the server sends Cache-Control: private, max-age=0. Permanent redirects can be remembered by clients; prefer the default for links whose destination or rules may change.

Social preview overrides

Link creation, bulk creation and editing accept a top-level og object:

{
  "url": "https://example.com/article",
  "og": {
    "title": "The article title",
    "description": "A short description for a shared link.",
    "image": "https://images.example.com/article-card.png"
  }
}

Configure at least one field. Titles are capped at 200 characters, descriptions at 500, and image URLs at 2,048. Empty fields and unknown keys are rejected. Images must use public HTTPS URLs without credentials. Shortn does not fetch or upload these images in the redirect path; social platforms fetch the configured URL. Use a stable image URL accessible without authentication.

PATCH /v1/links/{id} replaces the whole og object when supplied. Send og: null to clear it; omit it to preserve existing metadata. Reads return the configured object. Creation and bulk creation share the same validation. Metadata mutations invalidate canonical and historical-alias cache entries.

Recognized preview UAs include facebookexternalhit, Facebot, Twitterbot, LinkedInBot, Slackbot-LinkExpanding, Discordbot, TelegramBot, WhatsApp, SkypeUriPreview, MicrosoftPreview, Pinterestbot and redditbot. Matching is case-insensitive and examines at most 2,000 characters. This is response selection, not crawler authentication; user-agent strings can be copied. Search crawlers and other automated clients retain normal redirects.

After safety, password, time and visit-limit gates, a preview bot gets private HTML with escaped Open Graph/Twitter metadata and a meta refresh to the selected web destination. The canonical og:url is the short URL without request query values. An omitted preview title falls back to the link's title. An omitted image does not invent an image URL. Device/country/rotation selection and query/UTM rules still apply, but preview responses do not set rotation cookies or open native apps. Humans keep normal redirect or deep-link behavior.

Recorded preview requests remain marked as bots in the click stream. They contribute to bot volume rather than human click/scan analytics, click webhooks or the hot visit count. Gate and fallback responses do not expose configured preview metadata. Responses vary by user agent and are private with zero freshness; platforms may keep their own preview cache and may require a fresh scrape after an edit. The advanced in-page preview editor remains pending.

Destination health

Link reads include read-only health results when a current check is scheduled. health.checks contains individual destination results; checkedAt is the last completed cycle and nextCheckAt is the next queued check time. An empty checks list means the first check is pending. Queued checks may run after their due time while a backlog drains.

The worker checks the main destination and configured web targets, including fallback, device/country/rotation URLs, HTTPS app links and store URLs. Custom app schemes are excluded. URLs differing only by fragment share a check. A cycle runs weekly, with one target checked per job and bounded batches for large libraries. Requests are limited per hostname across worker instances.

Checks use HEAD, falling back to GET with a one-byte Range request for HTTP 405 or 501. The connection closes after response headers, even if a server ignores Range. Up to three redirects are followed, with public-address validation and DNS pinning on every hop. Private, mixed public/private DNS and credential-bearing targets are not requested. Redirect loops, DNS/network failures and timeouts produce an unknown/unreachable result, not an assumed HTTP error.

Each check reports status (ok, http_error, unreachable, blocked), optional HTTP status, check time, consecutive HTTP-error streak, and failingSince. health.flagged becomes true after two consecutive 4xx/5xx checks of any target. A healthy response clears that target's streak. Network/blocked outcomes do not pretend that the page returned a 4xx/5xx status. Failure codes exclude remote response bodies and credentials.

Health is informational: results never disable a link, change safety status or modify its redirect. Websites may treat the checker differently from a browser. The checker identifies itself as Shortn-LinkHealth/1.0, and Shortn treats its requests as bots so checks of other Shortn links do not inflate human analytics. Changing the destination set resets the check generation and hides old results; late results cannot apply to an edited link. Metadata-only edits retain results.

The same workspace permissions and link-read API scopes apply. Health fields cannot be written through link mutations. Active dashboard rows flag repeated HTTP errors and open the link overview's Destination health section. It shows per-target status and check dates, distinguishes blocked and unreachable results, and hides stale results after a destination edit. Health remains informational.

Dashboard Links and QR selections persist across pages and filters, up to 500 items per action. Delete opens the existing permission-checked review page. This dashboard limit is separate from the REST bulk-create limit of 1,000.

Remaining rule features

Unsupported rule fields are rejected. The advanced in-page rule editor also remains pending. Background safety scans for new or changed link destinations are durable: the worker executes them through BullMQ, retries failures with bounded exponential backoff, and rescans successful links weekly. A destination edit supersedes any older queued or running request. WEB_RISK_API_KEY must be configured in the worker for Google Web Risk checks; without it the existing structural/domain-age checks still run. A configured reputation-provider outage is retried rather than treated as a completed weekly scan.

Safety-provider results use shared Redis caching. RDAP registration timestamps are cached per destination host for 24 hours; domain age is recalculated for each scan. Web Risk threat matches remain specific to the exact URL and expire at the provider's expireTime, following the Lookup API cache protocol. Clean Lookup responses and provider failures are not cached. A clean path does not establish trust for other URLs on that host. Cache outages fall through to provider checks, and configured reputation outages retain durable retries.

mcp.title: MCP setup and implementation status
mcp.markdown:
# MCP setup and implementation status

Shortn has a locally verified MCP endpoint at `/mcp`, using the official
TypeScript SDK's Streamable HTTP transport with JSON responses. Deployment is
disabled by default. API-key access and workspace OAuth consent are implemented
and verified locally. Manual supported-client and staging acceptance remain
open. These examples apply to an explicitly enabled deployment.

## Authentication and rollout

Use a scoped workspace API key as `Authorization: Bearer sk_live_…`. Session
cookies are not accepted. Current membership, role, expiry, IP restrictions and
revocation are checked on every request. MCP and REST share the same per-key
rate budget and `RateLimit-*` headers. Core services enforce resource permissions.

Operators enable `PLATFORM_MCP_ENABLED=1` and configure `MCP_PUBLIC_ORIGIN`,
`API_KEY_PEPPER`, and both Redis URLs. Production requires HTTPS and separate
cache/durable Redis instances. `PLATFORM_MCP_ROLLOUT` starts at zero; the
workspace's `platformFeatures.mcp` override takes precedence. MCP's gate is
independent of REST. The request Host must match the configured public host;
cross-origin browser requests are not enabled by this API-key implementation.

## Workspace OAuth

Enable `MCP_OAUTH_ENABLED=1` on both web and API, with the same
`MCP_PUBLIC_ORIGIN`. On the API, set `MCP_OAUTH_ISSUER` to the web auth issuer,
for example `https://app.shortn.at/api/auth`, and enable the MCP mount as above.
Production requires HTTPS. Keep the web and API workspace rollout configuration
consistent. OAuth remains disabled unless explicitly configured.

The API publishes `/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/mcp` and includes its
address in the unauthenticated `WWW-Authenticate` challenge. The web publishes
`/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server/api/auth`. Clients discover the
provider and register a public client, then request an authorization code for
the exact MCP resource (`https://api.shortn.at/mcp`) with PKCE S256. The browser
asks the user to sign in, select an eligible workspace and review permissions.
Email and username sign-in both resume the connection. Cancel creates no grant.

A grant is limited by the user's current workspace role and requested scopes.
Access tokens expire after ten minutes; refresh requires `offline_access`.
Client, consent, membership and the originating login session are checked live;
signing out of that session ends access. Workspace selection changes between
review and approval are rejected. OAuth mutation audit actors identify the
verified client. Refresh preserves the rate-limit identity.

Registered callbacks must match exactly. HTTPS, loopback HTTP and supported
native/private-use callback schemes are accepted; callbacks with credentials
or fragments are rejected. Native client launch and Claude Desktop acceptance
have not yet been verified. The local browser fixture verifies discovery,
consent, PKCE exchange and an authenticated MCP call against a synthetic app.

## Tools and scopes

| Tool              | Required scopes                                                                  | Behavior                                                                |
| ----------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `create_link`     | `links:write`                                                                    | URL, optional key/domain/title/tags/UTM/expiry; returns a short URL     |
| `update_link`     | `links:write`                                                                    | Updates fields and rules by ID                                          |
| `archive_link`    | `links:write`                                                                    | Moves authorized links to 30-day trash; annotated destructive           |
| `get_link`        | `links:read`                                                                     | Reads by ID or key; custom domains can be specified                     |
| `search_links`    | `links:read`; `campaigns:read` for a campaign filter                             | Query/tag/campaign filters, up to 200 results and a next cursor         |
| `get_analytics`   | `analytics:read`; `links:read` for a link key or `campaigns:read` for a campaign | One link, tag, campaign or workspace; bounded breakdown and summary     |
| `create_qr_code`  | `qr:write`, `links:read`                                                         | Attaches a QR code; signed export URL or asynchronous export job when enabled         |
| `get_qr_export` | `qr:read` | Reads export progress and the finished expiring private download URL |
| `list_campaigns`  | `campaigns:read`                                                                 | Bounded cursor pages without full campaign link libraries               |
| `create_campaign` | `campaigns:write`                                                                | Creates a campaign                                                      |
| `add_bio_link`    | `bio:write`, `links:write`                                                       | Creates and appends atomically; a full/missing page rolls back creation |
| `get_usage`       | `workspace:read`                                                                 | Current period consumption and plan limits                              |

Wildcard scopes such as `qr:*` and `bio:*` include their read/write scopes.
Scoped viewers cannot mutate resources; members can archive only their own
links. Analytics retain plan and retention limits. Search and campaign listings
use server-side pagination: follow `nextCursor` to browse the full library.
Tool errors have stable codes and `isError: true`.

`create_qr_code` returns a signed `exportUrl` when the enabled worker finishes
within its bounded wait, or an `exportJobId` to poll. The added
`get_qr_export` tool requires `qr:read` and returns the finished private URL.
See [QR exports](/docs/qr-exports.md) for flags, formats, limits and remaining UI
and staging gates. Disabled export configuration reports `exportStatus: "disabled"`.

Mutations record durable intent in `audit_log` before calling core, with actor
`mcp:api-key:{keyId}`, real user ID and tool name, followed by succeeded/failed
status. If intent recording fails, the mutation does not run. If completion
recording fails after success, intent remains for reconciliation and the tool
retains its successful response to avoid encouraging a duplicate mutation.
Audit records omit raw arguments, destination URLs and secrets.

## Resources and prompts

- `shortn://links/{key}`: default-domain link; requires `links:read`.
- `shortn://analytics/summary`: last seven days; requires `analytics:read`.
- `weekly_link_report`: prompt to summarize that resource.
- `create_campaign_links`: prompt taking `title` and `urls` strings.

Prompts describe work; fetching one does not mutate data. Custom-domain links
use `get_link` with `domain` instead of the default-domain resource.

## Client configuration

Replace the origin below with the enabled deployment's origin. Create a key
with the scopes needed for the workflow.

For [Claude Code](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/mcp), set `SHORTN_API_KEY` in
your shell and add the HTTP server:

```sh
claude mcp add --transport http shortn https://api.shortn.at/mcp \
  --header "Authorization: Bearer ${SHORTN_API_KEY}"
```

For [Cursor](https://cursor.com/docs/mcp), use `.cursor/mcp.json` and provide
`SHORTN_API_KEY` in the environment used to start Cursor:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "shortn": {
      "url": "https://api.shortn.at/mcp",
      "headers": { "Authorization": "Bearer ${env:SHORTN_API_KEY}" }
    }
  }
}
```

For [VS Code](https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/agents/reference/mcp-configuration),
use `.vscode/mcp.json` with a masked input:

```json
{
  "inputs": [
    {
      "type": "promptString",
      "id": "shortnApiKey",
      "description": "Shortn API key",
      "password": true
    }
  ],
  "servers": {
    "shortn": {
      "type": "http",
      "url": "https://api.shortn.at/mcp",
      "headers": { "Authorization": "Bearer ${input:shortnApiKey}" }
    }
  }
}
```

These follow the clients' documented HTTP/header formats. Local verification
uses the SDK client and MCP Inspector; manual client and staging acceptance
remain open. OAuth-capable clients can use the discovery flow above on an
explicitly enabled deployment; native client acceptance is still pending.

qr-exports.title: QR exports
qr-exports.markdown:
# QR exports

QR exports are implemented and verified locally. They are disabled by default;
external storage and staging acceptance remain open. The worker produces SVG,
PNG and print-sized PDF artifacts from an immutable design snapshot. Single and
selected ZIP dashboard exports include review, progress and private downloads.

## Enablement

Set `QR_EXPORTS_ENABLED=1` on the web dashboard, API and worker. Each requires
`S3_ENDPOINT`, `S3_REGION`, `S3_BUCKET`, `S3_ACCESS_KEY_ID` and
`S3_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY`, pointing at the same private S3/R2-compatible bucket.
The worker also requires `APP_URL`; `APP_URL` and optional `PUBLIC_ORIGIN`
define the allowed origins of stored upload logos. Production origins require
HTTPS. Provision the declared job indexes with `bun run db:indexes` and run the
worker with the existing durable Redis configuration. REST and MCP retain their
independent mount and workspace rollout gates.

The public assets route serves only validated `uploads/` keys. Export objects
under `exports/qr/` are delivered by signatures after authorization. Keep this
cache prefix private and available for every active job's delivery lifetime;
job access and signatures expire after 24 hours. ZIP output under
`exports/jobs/qr/` needs a 24-hour lifecycle; it must also remain private.

## REST

Use a bearer API key with `qr:read`. Viewers can export codes they can read.
Exporting does not edit the QR code or require `qr:write`.

```sh
curl --max-redirs 0 -i \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${SHORTN_API_KEY}" \
  'https://api.shortn.at/v1/qr-codes/QR_ID/export?format=png&size=1024'
```

`format` is `svg`, `png` or `pdf` (default `svg`); `size` is an integer from
128 through 4096 pixels (default 1024). `202 Accepted` returns an export job and
an authenticated polling path in `Location`, with `Retry-After: 1`:

```json
{
  "id": "JOB_ID",
  "state": "pending",
  "format": "png",
  "size": 1024,
  "createdAt": "2026-10-15T10:00:00.000Z",
  "expiresAt": "2026-10-16T10:00:00.000Z"
}
```

Poll `GET /v1/qr-exports/JOB_ID` using the same workspace credential. The status
is `pending`, `running`, `completed` or `failed`. Completed jobs include
`downloadUrl`, `downloadExpiresAt` and print guidance. The download URL is a
private attachment signature valid only for the remaining job lifetime. A
repeated export request redirects with `303 See Other` when ready; use `curl -L`
to follow that redirect and save the artifact. Cross-origin clients can read
`Location`, `Retry-After` and rate headers. Status responses use
`Cache-Control: private, no-store` and omit the stored design and object key.

Equivalent requests for the same creator/design/format/size in the same UTC day
reuse the job. The worker retries temporary storage failures and resumes expired
leases. New requests after a design change produce a new snapshot. A failed
print design returns a stable failure code; repeated export requests return
`409 export_failed` with the job ID and reason. Temporary signing failure returns
`503 storage_unavailable`. Expired, foreign or inaccessible jobs return `404`;
revoked credentials return `401`.

## Dashboard

From a QR code, choose **Export for print**, then SVG, PNG or PDF and a size
from 128 to 4096 px. The preview uses corrected print options, and the page shows
minimum print guidance. JPEG remains available separately for screen use. With
the flag off, existing browser downloads remain available.

In the QR library, select codes across pages and filters and choose
**Export selected**. Viewers can export readable codes. The review supports the
library’s searchable tag, date and keyword filters, date grouping and 25-row
server pages. Filters change the review list; the ZIP includes the entire
selection shown in the count, up to 500 codes and 512 MiB. A short, private
selection reference is bound to the current workspace and user for 24 hours.

The status page polls while visible, shows preparation counts, and stops polling
when the job completes or fails. It provides a private attachment download and
its expiry, or a clear error and a link to review a failing design. Current
membership and resource access are rechecked on each request. A selection that
loses an item before submission is rejected without creating a job.

## Selected QR ZIP

`POST /v1/qr-codes/export` queues a ZIP job with `qr:read`, including for viewers.
Send `ids` (1–500 selected QR IDs), `format` (`svg`, `png` or `pdf`) and optional
`size` (128–4096, default 1024). Duplicate IDs are collapsed; every selected code
must belong to the workspace. A mixed foreign/missing selection creates no job.
Use `Idempotency-Key` for request replay. Equivalent selections, independent of
order, reuse the same creator/day/design job.

The 202 response includes the job ID, `total`, `done`, the 500-code `limit`, and
`maximumBytes: 536870912` (512 MiB). Poll the authenticated `Location` at
`GET /v1/qr-exports/zip/JOB_ID`. `phase` is `rendering` or `assembling`; `done`
counts checkpointed artifacts. The worker persists one immutable item snapshot
per selected code, processes cursor batches, and resumes completed items after
retry or lease recovery. ZIP names are safe, unique flat filenames. A print
failure identifies `failedQrId` and its stable reason.

Archives stream to private multipart storage rather than accumulating the
entire ZIP in worker memory. Output above 512 MiB fails as `archive_too_large`
and incomplete multipart uploads are aborted. A completed status includes the
expiring attachment URL. Current membership and every selected resource are
checked before signing; foreign, deleted or expired selections cannot be
retrieved. Configure a 24-hour lifecycle for `exports/jobs/qr/`, separately from
the reusable design cache under `exports/qr/`.

## MCP

`create_qr_code` accepts optional `format` and `size` alongside `linkKey`,
`domain` and `style`. It requires `qr:write` and `links:read`. With exports enabled,
it waits up to five seconds for the worker and returns the signed `exportUrl`
when ready. If still processing, it returns `exportJobId`, `exportStatus` and a
null `exportUrl`. Poll `get_qr_export {id: exportJobId}` with `qr:read` to obtain
the finished download URL. This is the twelfth tool, added to the eleven planned
workspace tools for asynchronous delivery.

When export configuration is disabled, QR creation still succeeds with
`exportStatus: "disabled"`. If export fails after QR creation, the result retains
the created QR ID and available job ID; it reports the export failure without
presenting the QR mutation as failed. Polling is read-only; QR creation retains
its mutation audit actor and record.

## Print output

Print plans enforce a quiet zone of at least four modules, error correction Q
minimum (H with a logo), opaque colors and at least 3:1 module/background contrast,
including finder colors and gradients. Six dot/finder styles, linear/radial
paints and stored PNG logos are supported. Sizes, payloads and logo bytes are
bounded. The worker reads logos directly from validated stored upload keys;
it does not fetch arbitrary image URLs.

PDF page dimensions preserve 300 dpi. `print.minimumMm` recommends a physical
size using four printer pixels per module at 300 dpi. Circular legacy designs currently fail explicitly. Frame/caption treatment
remains unimplemented. The local parity fixture verifies corrected

qr-exports.html:
QR exports

QR exports are implemented and verified locally. They are disabled by default; external storage and staging acceptance remain open. The worker produces SVG, PNG and print-sized PDF artifacts from an immutable design snapshot. Single and selected ZIP dashboard exports include review, progress and private downloads.

Enablement

Set QR_EXPORTS_ENABLED=1 on the web dashboard, API and worker. Each requires S3_ENDPOINT, S3_REGION, S3_BUCKET, S3_ACCESS_KEY_ID and S3_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY, pointing at the same private S3/R2-compatible bucket. The worker also requires APP_URL; APP_URL and optional PUBLIC_ORIGIN define the allowed origins of stored upload logos. Production origins require HTTPS. Provision the declared job indexes with bun run db:indexes and run the worker with the existing durable Redis configuration. REST and MCP retain their independent mount and workspace rollout gates.

The public assets route serves only validated uploads/ keys. Export objects under exports/qr/ are delivered by signatures after authorization. Keep this cache prefix private and available for every active job's delivery lifetime; job access and signatures expire after 24 hours. ZIP output under exports/jobs/qr/ needs a 24-hour lifecycle; it must also remain private.

REST

Use a bearer API key with qr:read. Viewers can export codes they can read. Exporting does not edit the QR code or require qr:write.

curl --max-redirs 0 -i \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${SHORTN_API_KEY}" \
  'https://api.shortn.at/v1/qr-codes/QR_ID/export?format=png&size=1024'

format is svg, png or pdf (default svg); size is an integer from 128 through 4096 pixels (default 1024). 202 Accepted returns an export job and an authenticated polling path in Location, with Retry-After: 1:

{
  "id": "JOB_ID",
  "state": "pending",
  "format": "png",
  "size": 1024,
  "createdAt": "2026-10-15T10:00:00.000Z",
  "expiresAt": "2026-10-16T10:00:00.000Z"
}

Poll GET /v1/qr-exports/JOB_ID using the same workspace credential. The status is pending, running, completed or failed. Completed jobs include downloadUrl, downloadExpiresAt and print guidance. The download URL is a private attachment signature valid only for the remaining job lifetime. A repeated export request redirects with 303 See Other when ready; use curl -L to follow that redirect and save the artifact. Cross-origin clients can read Location, Retry-After and rate headers. Status responses use Cache-Control: private, no-store and omit the stored design and object key.

Equivalent requests for the same creator/design/format/size in the same UTC day reuse the job. The worker retries temporary storage failures and resumes expired leases. New requests after a design change produce a new snapshot. A failed print design returns a stable failure code; repeated export requests return 409 export_failed with the job ID and reason. Temporary signing failure returns 503 storage_unavailable. Expired, foreign or inaccessible jobs return 404; revoked credentials return 401.

Dashboard

From a QR code, choose Export for print, then SVG, PNG or PDF and a size from 128 to 4096 px. The preview uses corrected print options, and the page shows minimum print guidance. JPEG remains available separately for screen use. With the flag off, existing browser downloads remain available.

In the QR library, select codes across pages and filters and choose Export selected. Viewers can export readable codes. The review supports the library’s searchable tag, date and keyword filters, date grouping and 25-row server pages. Filters change the review list; the ZIP includes the entire selection shown in the count, up to 500 codes and 512 MiB. A short, private selection reference is bound to the current workspace and user for 24 hours.

The status page polls while visible, shows preparation counts, and stops polling when the job completes or fails. It provides a private attachment download and its expiry, or a clear error and a link to review a failing design. Current membership and resource access are rechecked on each request. A selection that loses an item before submission is rejected without creating a job.

Selected QR ZIP

POST /v1/qr-codes/export queues a ZIP job with qr:read, including for viewers. Send ids (1–500 selected QR IDs), format (svg, png or pdf) and optional size (128–4096, default 1024). Duplicate IDs are collapsed; every selected code must belong to the workspace. A mixed foreign/missing selection creates no job. Use Idempotency-Key for request replay. Equivalent selections, independent of order, reuse the same creator/day/design job.

The 202 response includes the job ID, total, done, the 500-code limit, and maximumBytes: 536870912 (512 MiB). Poll the authenticated Location at GET /v1/qr-exports/zip/JOB_ID. phase is rendering or assembling; done counts checkpointed artifacts. The worker persists one immutable item snapshot per selected code, processes cursor batches, and resumes completed items after retry or lease recovery. ZIP names are safe, unique flat filenames. A print failure identifies failedQrId and its stable reason.

Archives stream to private multipart storage rather than accumulating the entire ZIP in worker memory. Output above 512 MiB fails as archive_too_large and incomplete multipart uploads are aborted. A completed status includes the expiring attachment URL. Current membership and every selected resource are checked before signing; foreign, deleted or expired selections cannot be retrieved. Configure a 24-hour lifecycle for exports/jobs/qr/, separately from the reusable design cache under exports/qr/.

MCP

create_qr_code accepts optional format and size alongside linkKey, domain and style. It requires qr:write and links:read. With exports enabled, it waits up to five seconds for the worker and returns the signed exportUrl when ready. If still processing, it returns exportJobId, exportStatus and a null exportUrl. Poll get_qr_export {id: exportJobId} with qr:read to obtain the finished download URL. This is the twelfth tool, added to the eleven planned workspace tools for asynchronous delivery.

When export configuration is disabled, QR creation still succeeds with exportStatus: "disabled". If export fails after QR creation, the result retains the created QR ID and available job ID; it reports the export failure without presenting the QR mutation as failed. Polling is read-only; QR creation retains its mutation audit actor and record.

Print output

Print plans enforce a quiet zone of at least four modules, error correction Q minimum (H with a logo), opaque colors and at least 3:1 module/background contrast, including finder colors and gradients. Six dot/finder styles, linear/radial paints and stored PNG logos are supported. Sizes, payloads and logo bytes are bounded. The worker reads logos directly from validated stored upload keys; it does not fetch arbitrary image URLs.

PDF page dimensions preserve 300 dpi. print.minimumMm recommends a physical size using four printer pixels per module at 300 dpi. Circular legacy designs currently fail explicitly. Frame/caption treatment remains unimplemented. The local parity fixture verifies corrected print previews against server artifacts at 1024 px.

webhooks.title: Outgoing webhooks
webhooks.markdown:
# Outgoing webhooks

Outgoing webhooks are implemented behind default-off flags. Main link CRUD,
trash/restore, managed bio publication and domain verification produce automatic
events. Campaign UTM changes and QR backing/attachment mutations also produce link
events. Tag rename/deletion, domain assignment/removal/recovery, safety scans and
report-triggered blocking also emit link updates. Opted-in clicks and scans are
batched. Import completion remains pending.
Explicit test requests produce `webhook.test` deliveries.

## Configure an endpoint

Use an API key with `webhooks:write` whose creator is a workspace owner or admin.
Creation, changes, tests and redelivery require `PLATFORM_WEBHOOKS_ENABLED=1`, a
configured `WEBHOOK_SECRET_KEY`, and an enabled workspace or rollout cohort.
Metadata reads require `webhooks:read` and an owner/admin creator. Reads and
removal remain available when outgoing provisioning is disabled.

`POST /v1/webhooks` accepts `name`, an HTTPS `url`, `events`, and optional
`enabled` (default true). Supported subscription names are `link.created`,
`link.updated`, `link.deleted`, `link.clicked`, `qr.scanned`, `bio.published`,
`domain.verified` and `import.completed`.

The creation response includes a `whsec_…` signing secret. Retain it securely;
subsequent metadata reads omit it. Replaying the original POST with the same
`Idempotency-Key` returns the original creation response. Signing secrets are
encrypted in MongoDB and creation-response idempotency records. Keep the same
encryption key across API and worker processes. Changing it requires a separate
re-encryption procedure; replacing it directly prevents existing secrets from
being decrypted.

Endpoints must use HTTPS without URL credentials or fragments. The delivery
worker rejects private, loopback, link-local, reserved and other special IP
ranges, including mixed public/private DNS answers. It pins a validated DNS
address while preserving TLS hostname verification, applies DNS and request
deadlines, and treats redirects as unsuccessful deliveries.

## Test, inspect and redeliver

`POST /v1/webhooks/{id}/test` returns HTTP 202 with the persisted delivery ID and
event ID. No destination request runs in the API handler. The worker sends:

```json
{
  "id": "event UUID",
  "type": "webhook.test",
  "createdAt": "2026-10-13T12:00:00.000Z",
  "workspaceId": "workspace ID",
  "data": {}
}
```

`GET /v1/webhooks/{id}/deliveries` returns a cursor-paginated log retained for 30
days. It includes status, attempt count, timestamps and bounded error codes,
without receiver response bodies or signing secrets. Use
`POST /v1/webhooks/{id}/deliveries/{deliveryId}/redeliver` to create a new delivery
for the same event. An expired log record cannot be redelivered.

Endpoint metadata uses `GET /v1/webhooks`, `GET/PATCH/DELETE /v1/webhooks/{id}`.
Lists accept `cursor`, `limit` (1–200, default 50) and literal `search` on name or
URL. Disabling or deleting an endpoint prevents queued deliveries from starting
another destination request; an already-started request may finish.

## Verify deliveries

Headers include `Shortn-Delivery-Id`, `Shortn-Event-Id` and
`Shortn-Signature: t={unix seconds},v1={hex HMAC-SHA256}`. The signed bytes are the
timestamp, a period, and the exact raw UTF-8 request body. Use the complete
`whsec_…` string as the HMAC key, without decoding or removing its prefix. Check
timestamp freshness and compare signatures with a constant-time comparison.

Delivery is at least once. Persist the event ID when processing an event so an
uncertain network response or manual redelivery cannot repeat an already-applied
operation. All attempts for a delivery retain its delivery and event IDs;
manual redelivery has a new delivery ID and the original event ID. Return a 2xx
status once the event has been durably accepted by the receiver.

MongoDB is the durable delivery source. BullMQ executes attempts on the durable
Redis instance. Failed attempts back off exponentially from one second, capped
at one hour, within a 24-hour retry window. Expired leases can be reclaimed after
a worker interruption. Endpoints with an unresolved failure period of three days
are disabled and a notification record is persisted atomically. When email is
configured, the worker emails the workspace owner in their preferred language,
retrying failed sends every five minutes with a stable provider idempotency key.
Each new disablement has a separate notification identity. The existing mail
allowlist applies. Workspace owners and admins can manage endpoints and delivery logs in Settings → Webhooks.

## Automatic mutation events

The mutation and source event commit together in a MongoDB transaction. Failed
mutations produce no event. No enabled subscriber means no source event is stored.
The worker fans out in bounded recipient pages, advancing its cursor atomically
with delivery creation. Concurrent pumps and restarts reuse automatic delivery
identities. Subscribers created after the event are excluded; subscriptions and
workspace feature gates are checked when fanout runs and before sending.

Main link creation emits `link.created`; edits and restoring a trashed link emit
`link.updated`; moving an active link to trash emits `link.deleted`. Repeating
delete/restore does not emit another transition event. Link `data` contains `id`,
`domain`, `key`, `url`, `title` and `deletedAt`, with no password material, safety
reports or visitor information. Managed publication emits `bio.published` with
`id`, `handle` and `revision`; republishing that revision is a no-op. A domain's
transition to active emits `domain.verified` with `id`, `hostname`, `kind` and
`status`; periodic verification does not repeat the event.

## Click and scan batches

Explicitly subscribe to `link.clicked` or `qr.scanned` to receive these events.
They are collected separately per workspace and event type, then sent when 100
receipts accumulate or the oldest receipt reaches 10 seconds. The worker checks
every second; queue or database backlog can delay delivery. One pump processes
at most 20 batches of 100 receipts, sharing capacity between due workspaces.

Batch `data` has `count` and an `events` array. Each entry has `id` (the original
stream ID), `linkId`, `timestamp`, `domain`, `key` and, for scans, `qrId`. Domain
and key strings are bounded. Raw IPs, user agents, referrers, query parameters
and visitor hashes are excluded. Bots are excluded. Legacy personal-workspace
links and legacy QR backing links are supported; QR ownership and backing-link
identity are checked before recording a scan.

Receipts commit with majority write concern before Redis acknowledgement. If
receipt persistence fails after analytics was saved, the pending entry replays
without duplicating analytics or webhook receipts. Receipt consumption and source
event creation share a transaction, so an interrupted batch can be retried.
Completed receipts retain their stream IDs for 30 days to deduplicate replays;
unprocessed receipts have no TTL. Automatic fanout uses the batch's first receipt
time to exclude endpoints created after collection started. Workspace and endpoint
disablement still apply when the batch is flushed and delivered.

Campaign UTM replacement, rename and deletion emit `link.updated` for links whose
variants change. Their events commit with campaign membership and canonical link
fields. References are workspace scoped, including legacy title-only references;
other campaign IDs with the same title are preserved. Repeating identical variants
emits no update. Stale expected-state edits return a conflict before creating a
campaign or recording an event.

Creating a QR emits `link.created` for its hidden backing link and `link.updated`
when attaching it to an existing link. QR editing emits updates for changed
backing/attached links, including tags when explicitly applied to the attachment.
Deleting a QR emits `link.deleted` for its removed backing link and `link.updated`
for detachment. QR, backing-link, attachment and source-event mutations share a
transaction; creation quota checks are serialized, and deletion archives legacy
scans in 1,000-row pages inside that transaction. Stored link IDs keep attachment
updates and detachment working after a linked resource is renamed. Legacy records
without those IDs retain their key-based lookup.

Tag rename and deletion emit `link.updated` for linked resources, including
trashed links and canonical tag-ID references. Repeating the current tag name is
a no-op. Tag/reference updates and source events share the existing transaction.
Workspace ownership checks exclude contaminated foreign references.

Domain assignment, removal and recovery emit updates for changed links. Assignment
checks hostname/TLS readiness and add-on status in its transaction, protects all
previous keys against collisions, and rejects trashed links. Domain operations
invalidate canonical and alias caches on affected hosts and queue related bio
page invalidations with the mutation. Recovery retains conflicting links on their
original host.

Safety scans emit updates when risk, status or blocking fields change. Periodic
rescans with identical state emit no event. A scan result for a changed destination
is discarded; fields derive from the current transactional document, preserving
concurrent password edits and report-triggered blocking. The third distinct abuse
report blocks the link and emits an update in the same transaction. Reports below
the threshold and duplicate reporters do not emit update events. Report details,
reporter identities and visitor data are excluded from event payloads.

## Workspace settings

Settings → Webhooks provides in-page create/edit forms, explicit event selection,
pause/enable controls, test requests and confirmed deletion. The signing secret
is shown once after creation; copy it and acknowledge saving it before creating
another endpoint. Refreshing or leaving the page removes the secret from the UI.
Endpoint lists support literal name/URL search and 25-row cursor pages.

Open an endpoint's Delivery log to view its 30-day history in 25-row pages.
Rows show event identity, state, attempts, HTTP status and bounded error codes.
Redeliver creates a new delivery for the same event, and Refresh updates the log.
Paused endpoints must be enabled before requesting deliveries. When outgoing
webhooks are unavailable, reads and deletion remain available; provisioning and
delivery requests are disabled. Server actions recheck the current workspace role
and shared service gates for every operation. Interface copy is available in
English, Portuguese and Spanish.

en/guides/analytics/understanding-analyt.title: Understanding analytics
en/guides/analytics/understanding-analyt.markdown:
# Understanding analytics

Shortn counts every visit to your short links and QR codes. This guide explains what is counted, how to narrow the numbers down with ranges, breakdowns and filters, how to export them, and how visitor data is protected.

## Clicks and scans

Shortn records two kinds of visit:

- a **click** is a visit through a short link, whether typed, tapped or opened from another site;
- a **scan** is a visit through one of your QR codes.

The **Type** filter switches between **Clicks and scans**, **Clicks** and **QR scans**. The summary at the top also shows **Unique visitors** and the **Top country**.

## Where to find analytics

- **Analytics** in the sidebar covers the whole workspace.
- A link's **Analytics** tab covers that link.
- A QR code's **Scans** tab covers that code.
- A campaign's **Analytics** tab covers the links in that campaign.
- A bio page's **Analytics** tab shows views, clicks and the click-through rate of the page.

All of them except bio pages share the same controls.

## Choose a date range

1. Open **Date range** and pick **Last 7 days**, **Last 30 days**, **Last 90 days** or **Last 12 months**, or set a **Custom range** with **From** and **To** dates.
2. Choose an **Interval** to group the chart by hour, day, week or month.

How far back you can go depends on your plan's analytics history. When a range starts earlier, the page tells you the date before which data is outside your plan's analytics window and shows what it can. See [Pricing](/en/pricing) for the history each plan includes.

## Breakdowns

Below the chart, breakdowns group visits by:

- **Links**
- **Countries** and **Cities**
- **Referrers**: the site a visit came from. Direct means no referring site, such as a typed address, an app or a QR scan.
- **Devices**, **Browsers** and **Operating systems**
- **UTM sources**, **UTM mediums** and **UTM campaigns**
- **Routing branches**: which redirect rule picked the destination, for links with country, device or rotation rules.

Each breakdown shows the top rows; select **See all** for the full list. Breakdowns other than links, and filtering by them, depend on your plan.

## Filter the view

Select a value in a breakdown to filter the whole page by it, or open the filters to combine several, for example one link, one country and mobile devices. Select **Clear all** to remove them.

Every filter is part of the page address, so you can bookmark a view or share it with a colleague who has access to the workspace.

## Export analytics

1. Set the range and filters you want.
2. Select **Export analytics**.
3. Under **Data**, choose **Aggregates** for totals per time bucket and per group, or **Raw events** for one row per visit.
4. Choose the format (CSV, or NDJSON for raw events) and select **Prepare export**.

Exports run in the background, so you can leave the page. Find finished files under **Export history**. Files and history expire 24 hours after preparation. The export keeps the retained window you reviewed, even if your plan changes before it runs. CSV export depends on your plan, and campaign export has its own plan requirement.

## Privacy

- Visitor IP addresses are hashed.
- Raw IP addresses are deleted after 90 days.
- Raw-event exports exclude IP addresses, visitor hashes and user agents.
- Embedded content on bio pages loads only after the visitor chooses to load it.

## Reading the numbers

- Compare the same range across links, rather than totals across ranges of different length.
- Use UTM breakdowns to see which channel worked, and routing branches to compare the destinations of one link.

## Next steps

- [UTM parameters](/docs/en/guides/links/utm-parameters)
- [Organizing campaigns](/docs/en/guides/campaigns/organizing-campaigns)
- [Upgrading plans](/docs/en/guides/billing/upgrading-plans)

How far back you can go depends on your plan's analytics history. When a range starts earlier, the page tells you the date before which data is outside your plan's analytics window and shows what it can. See Pricing for the history each plan includes.

Breakdowns

Below the chart, breakdowns group visits by:

  • Links
  • Countries and Cities
  • Referrers: the site a visit came from. Direct means no referring site, such as a typed address, an app or a QR scan.
  • Devices, Browsers and Operating systems
  • UTM sources, UTM mediums and UTM campaigns
  • Routing branches: which redirect rule picked the destination, for links with country, device or rotation rules.

Each breakdown shows the top rows; select See all for the full list. Breakdowns other than links, and filtering by them, depend on your plan.

Filter the view

Select a value in a breakdown to filter the whole page by it, or open the filters to combine several, for example one link, one country and mobile devices. Select Clear all to remove them.

Every filter is part of the page address, so you can bookmark a view or share it with a colleague who has access to the workspace.

Export analytics

  1. Set the range and filters you want.
  2. Select Export analytics.
  3. Under Data, choose Aggregates for totals per time bucket and per group, or Raw events for one row per visit.
  4. Choose the format (CSV, or NDJSON for raw events) and select Prepare export.

Exports run in the background, so you can leave the page. Find finished files under Export history. Files and history expire 24 hours after preparation. The export keeps the retained window you reviewed, even if your plan changes before it runs. CSV export depends on your plan, and campaign export has its own plan requirement.

Privacy

  • Visitor IP addresses are hashed.
  • Raw IP addresses are deleted after 90 days.
  • Raw-event exports exclude IP addresses, visitor hashes and user agents.
  • Embedded content on bio pages loads only after the visitor chooses to load it.

Reading the numbers

  • Compare the same range across links, rather than totals across ranges of different length.
  • Use UTM breakdowns to see which channel worked, and routing branches to compare the destinations of one link.

Next steps

  • UTM parameters
  • Organizing campaigns
  • Upgrading plans

en/guides/billing/upgrading-plans.title: Upgrading plans
en/guides/billing/upgrading-plans.markdown:
# Upgrading plans

Each workspace has its own plan. This guide covers where to see your plan and usage, how to upgrade, downgrade or cancel, how payment works, and what happens to your links when a plan changes. Only the workspace owner can change the plan or see invoices.

## See your plan and usage

Open **Settings** and select **Billing**. The page has three parts:

- **Plan**: your current plan and when it renews or ends. On Free, it shows when usage resets.
- **Usage**: links and QR codes created this period, and bio pages in total, against your plan's limits.
- **Invoices**: your payment history, with a **Download** link for each invoice.

Link and QR code limits reset every billing period. When you reach a limit, the page tells you, and you can upgrade to keep creating.

## Compare plans

Select **Compare plans** to see every plan side by side: limits, analytics history, members, workspaces and features such as custom keys, campaigns, analytics breakdowns, CSV export and QR logos. The same information is on the [Pricing](/en/pricing) page.

## Prices and currency

Plans are monthly and billed in US dollars. Shortn shows a euro estimate next to each price, based on European Central Bank reference rates. Checkout charges the dollar amount; the euro figure is only an estimate.

## Upgrade

1. Open **Compare plans**.
2. Select **Upgrade to …** on the plan you want.
3. On Free, you go to checkout. Enter your payment details there and confirm.
4. Back in Shortn, the billing page shows your new plan within a few seconds, once the payment provider confirms it. Select **Refresh** if it hasn't changed yet.

If you already pay for a plan, an upgrade opens a confirmation page instead of checkout. Select **Switch to …** to confirm. The new plan starts as soon as the billing provider confirms, and you are charged the prorated difference for the current period.

## Downgrade

1. Open **Compare plans** and select **Switch to …** on a lower plan.
2. Read the confirmation page, then select **Switch to …**.

You keep your current plan until the end of the period. The lower plan's limits and features apply from then on. To stay on your current plan, select **Keep …** instead.

## Cancel

1. On the billing page, select **Cancel plan**.
2. Confirm on the next page.

You keep the plan until the end of the current period; then the workspace moves to Free. Until that date you can select **Keep …** to resume the plan as usual.

## Your links keep working

Plan limits only control what you can create. When you downgrade or cancel, existing links, QR codes and bio pages keep redirecting. Features your new plan doesn't include stop being available for new changes. For example, if your plan no longer includes QR logos, you can keep an existing logo or remove it, but not add a new one.

## Payment methods and failed payments

Select **Open billing portal** to update your billing details or payment method. If a payment fails, the billing page shows a notice with **Update payment method**, so you can keep your plan.

## Custom-domain add-on

Custom domains are sold as an add-on, separate from the plan. Each add-on includes one domain. Buy one from **Settings** under **Domains** with **Buy domain add-on**, then connect the domain there. See [Customizing bio pages](/docs/en/guides/bio-pages/customizing-bio-pages).

## Enterprise

Enterprise plans have terms agreed with Shortn. To change one, contact Shortn.

## Next steps

- [Pricing](/en/pricing)
- [Getting started](/docs/en/guides/getting-started)

en/guides/bio-pages/creating-bio-pages.title: Creating bio pages
en/guides/bio-pages/creating-bio-pages.markdown:
# Creating bio pages

A bio page gathers your links on one public page, the kind you put in a social media profile. Visitors see your profile, your links and any other sections you add, and every click is counted. This guide covers creating a page and publishing its first version.

## Before you start

How many bio pages a workspace can have depends on your plan; the Bio pages list shows how many you've used. The links on a bio page are ordinary Shortn links, so they show up in **Links** and in analytics like any other link.

## Create a page

1. Open **Bio pages** in the sidebar and select **New bio page**.
2. Under **Address**, enter the address people will visit. Use 3 to 63 lowercase letters, numbers and hyphens. Shortn checks whether it's free as you type.
3. Optionally enter a **Title**, shown at the top of the page. If you leave it empty, the address is used.
4. Optionally select **Choose a link** under **First link** to put one of your links on the page straight away.
5. Select **Create page**.

The page's overview opens, with **Copy URL** and **Open page** for its public address.

## Build the page

From the overview, select **Edit bio page**. The editor shows a live preview of your page; switch between **Phone preview** and **Desktop preview** to check both.

1. Select **Add section** and choose what to add. The section types are **Profile**, **Link**, **Social links**, **Section heading**, **Text**, **Image**, **Embed**, **QR code** and **Links**.
2. Select a section in the preview to edit it. Drag its handle to reorder sections.
3. To add several of your links at once, add a **Links** section and select **Manage links**. You can filter by tags, search, and select links across pages before adding them.
4. To add a URL that isn't a short link yet, type it into a link section and select **Shorten and add link**. This creates a new link in your workspace.

Changes save as a draft while you work. Visitors don't see them until you publish.

## Publish

Select **Publish** when the draft is ready. The page is live at its address straight away. Each publish creates a version you can go back to later; see [Customizing bio pages](/docs/en/guides/bio-pages/customizing-bio-pages).

## Share the page

Select **Copy URL** on the overview and paste the address into your social profiles, email signature or printed material. To change the page's name in its address, open **Page settings** in the editor and use **Change handle**. Previous addresses keep working after a change.

## Bio page analytics

The **Analytics** tab of a bio page shows the last 30 days: **Views**, **Clicks**, **Click-through rate**, **Clicks by block** and the top referrers. The links on the page are also counted in the workspace **Analytics** page.

## Delete a page

On the overview, select **Delete bio page** and confirm. The public address stops working right away and becomes free for anyone to claim. The links that were on the page keep working.

## Tips

- Put the link that matters most first, or highlight it.
- Keep button text short so it fits on a phone.
- Check the phone preview before you publish, since bio pages are usually opened from a social app on a phone.

## Next steps

- [Customizing bio pages](/docs/en/guides/bio-pages/customizing-bio-pages)
- [Managing links](/docs/en/guides/links/managing-links)

en/guides/bio-pages/customizing-bio-page.title: Customizing bio pages
en/guides/bio-pages/customizing-bio-page.markdown:
# Customizing bio pages

The bio page editor works on a draft: you change sections, theme and settings, check the live preview, and publish when you're ready. This guide covers each part of the editor, scheduling, versions and connecting your own domain.

Open a bio page and select **Edit bio page**. The toolbar has **Add section**, **Sections**, **Theme**, **Page settings** and **History**.

## Sections

Select **Add section** to add one of these:

- **Profile**: avatar, title, description and alignment. You can choose the avatar shape.
- **Link**: one button for a link. Turn on **Highlight this link** to make it stand out, and add a thumbnail.
- **Links**: a group of links. Select **Manage links** to filter by tags, search, select links across pages and add them in one step. Under **Display links**, choose a layout such as a vertical list, paginated cards or image grids.
- **Social links**: icons that link to your profiles on other platforms.
- **Section heading** and **Text**: headings and short paragraphs between your links.
- **Image**: an image with a description and an optional link.
- **Embed**: content from YouTube, Spotify, SoundCloud, Vimeo or Apple Music. Visitors see a button to load it, with a note that loading the content shares their IP address with the provider.
- **QR code**: a QR code for one of your links.

Select a section in the preview to edit it, and drag its handle to reorder. **Sections** lists every section in order.

## Show sections on a schedule

Each section has a **Visible** switch and optional **Show from (UTC)** and **Show until (UTC)** dates. Use them to show a ticket link only during an event, or hide a section without deleting it. Scheduling is available on paid plans.

## Theme

Open **Theme** to change how the page looks:

1. Pick a **Preset theme** as a starting point, or choose **Custom**.
2. Adjust the colours: **Background**, **Surface**, **Text** and **Accent**.
3. Choose a **Font**, a **Button style**, a **Corner radius** and the **Spacing**.
4. Optionally add a **Cover image (optional)** behind the profile.

Themes are constrained so pages stay readable. If the text contrast is too low, the editor tells you so; select **Use accessible color** to fix it.

## Page settings

**Page settings** holds the settings that apply to the whole page:

- **Handle**: the name in the page's address. Select **Change handle** to rename it; previous addresses keep working.
- **Page language**: the language the page is written in.
- **Hide Shortn footer**: removes the "Made with Shortn" footer. Available on paid plans.
- **Search appearance**: turn on **Hide from search engines** to keep the page out of search results.

## Drafts and publishing

Your changes save as a draft a moment after you stop typing, and you can save at any time with **Save draft**. The preview shows the draft; visitors keep seeing the published page until you select **Publish**.

If the page was changed in another session, the editor warns you before saving, so you don't overwrite someone else's work.

## Versions

Every publish creates a version. Open **History** to see **Published versions (last 20)**. To go back, select **Restore version … to draft** on the one you want. The version is copied into your draft; select **Publish** to make it live again.

## Use your own domain

You can serve a bio page from your own domain, such as `links.example.com`, with the custom-domain add-on. Each add-on includes one domain.

1. Open **Settings** and select **Domains**.
2. If you don't have a free domain allowance, select **Buy domain add-on**.
3. Under **Add domain**, enter the **Hostname**, choose what to **Use for**, pick the **Bio page**, and select **Add domain**.
4. Follow the **DNS instructions**: create the CNAME record shown at your DNS provider. For an apex domain, use CNAME flattening.
5. Wait for the status to change to **Active**. If verification fails, check the record and select **Retry verification**.

Only people who can manage billing can add domains.

## Next steps

- [Creating bio pages](/docs/en/guides/bio-pages/creating-bio-pages)
- [Upgrading plans](/docs/en/guides/billing/upgrading-plans)

en/guides/campaigns/organizing-campaigns.title: Organizing campaigns
en/guides/campaigns/organizing-campaigns.markdown:
# Organizing campaigns

A campaign groups the UTM-tagged variants of your links so you can read their clicks together. Its title is the `utm_campaign` value, it stores suggested values for the other UTM parameters, and its UTM builder tags many links in one step. Campaigns depend on your plan; if yours doesn't include them, the Campaigns page says which plan does.

## Create a campaign

1. Open **Campaigns** in the sidebar and select **New campaign**.
2. Enter a **Title**. It is used as `utm_campaign` in the URLs you tag, so write it the way it should read in your analytics, for example `spring-sale`.
3. Optionally add a **Description**.
4. Select **Create campaign**.

The campaign opens with the tabs **Overview**, **Analytics**, **UTM builder** and **Settings**.

## Set UTM defaults

Open **Settings** and fill in the **UTM defaults**: lists of suggested sources, mediums, terms and contents. Type a value and press Enter to add it. Values are saved in lowercase. The UTM builder and the link variant form suggest them, which keeps spelling consistent across your team.

Renaming the campaign switches saved variants to the new title. URLs you have already shared keep the old title, and their clicks stop counting in the campaign.

## Add links with the UTM builder

1. Open **UTM builder**, or select **Build a tagged URL** on the overview.
2. Under **Links**, select **Browse links**. Filter by tags, search, or group results by tag. Tick links on as many pages as you need, or use **Select all results**, then select **Use … selected links**.
3. Fill in **Source**, **Medium** and, optionally, **Term** and **Content**. `utm_campaign` is always the campaign's title.
4. Check the **Tagged URL** preview and select **Copy URL** if you need it straight away.
5. Select **Save as variant**. With several links selected, the button saves the same variant on every one.

A link joins the campaign when one of its UTM variants uses the campaign. Until you save the variant, its clicks don't count in the campaign.

You can also add variants one link at a time from the link's **UTM variants** tab; see [UTM parameters](/docs/en/guides/links/utm-parameters).

## Move existing links into a campaign

From **Links**, select the links you want, across pages and filters, and choose **Move to campaign**. Pick the **Destination campaign** and select **Move selected links**. Each UTM variant keeps its source, medium, term and content, and the campaign's defaults don't overwrite them.

## Read campaign results

The **Overview** shows the last 30 days of clicks, scans and visitors, and **Links and variants** lists each link with its tagged URLs and clicks. Select **Copy utm_campaign** to copy the exact value.

The **Analytics** tab opens the full analytics filtered to the campaign, with the same date ranges, breakdowns and filters as the workspace **Analytics** page. Exporting a campaign's analytics as CSV depends on your plan. See [Understanding analytics](/docs/en/guides/analytics/understanding-analytics).

## Find campaigns

The Campaigns list has a **Search** field for titles and descriptions, and **Sort by** options for newest, oldest, most links or title.

## Delete a campaign

On the overview, select **Delete campaign** and confirm. Its UTM variants are removed from the links, and its UTM defaults are deleted. The links themselves keep working. URLs already shared with its `utm_campaign` keep their clicks, but no campaign page shows them any more.

## Tips

- Agree on a naming scheme for titles, such as `season-year-product`, before the team starts tagging.
- Use `utm_content` to compare placements of the same link inside one channel.

## Next steps

- [UTM parameters](/docs/en/guides/links/utm-parameters)
- [Understanding analytics](/docs/en/guides/analytics/understanding-analytics)

en/guides/getting-started.title: Getting started with Shortn
en/guides/getting-started.markdown:
# Getting started with Shortn

Shortn turns long URLs into short links you can share, print as QR codes or collect on a bio page, and it counts every click and scan. This guide covers creating an account, finding your way around the dashboard and creating your first short link.

## Create your account

1. Go to [app.shortn.at/register](https://app.shortn.at/register).
2. Enter your full name, a username, your email and a password, then select **Create account**. If the page offers **Continue with Google** or **Continue with GitHub**, you can use one of those instead.
3. Open the verification email and follow its link. The link works for one hour. If it has expired, or the email didn't arrive, request a new one with **Resend email**.
4. Sign in at [app.shortn.at/login](https://app.shortn.at/login) with your email or username.

Your account starts with a personal workspace on the Free plan.

## Find your way around

The sidebar holds the main sections of the dashboard:

- **Links**: every short link in the workspace, with search, tag filters, archive and trash.
- **Analytics**: clicks and QR scans across the workspace.
- **QR codes**: codes you design, download and print.
- **Bio pages**: link-in-bio pages with their own public address.
- **Campaigns**: groups of UTM-tagged links that you read together.
- **Settings**: workspace details, members, billing, domains, API keys and your account.

The **Usage** panel shows how much of your plan's monthly allowance you have used, for example **Links this month**.

A few keyboard shortcuts speed things up outside text fields: Ctrl+K (Cmd+K on a Mac) opens the **Command palette**, C starts a new link, and ? lists every shortcut under **Keyboard shortcuts**.

You can change the dashboard language and theme from the account menu.

## Create your first short link

1. Open **Links** in the sidebar.
2. Select **New link**, or paste a URL anywhere on the Links page outside a text field. Either way, the new-link form opens.
3. Enter the **Destination URL**. Shortn looks up the page and can suggest a title and key; select **Use page title** or **Use suggested key** to accept them.
4. Select **Create link**.

The link is created and copied to your clipboard, and its overview page opens. From there you can copy it again with **Copy short link**, open its **Analytics** tab or create a QR code for it. [Creating links](/docs/en/guides/links/creating-links) covers every field on the form.

## Work with a team

Each workspace has its own links, members and billing. To add a team workspace, open **Settings**, go to **General** and select **Create workspace** under **Team workspaces**. You become its owner and can invite people under **Members**. Members have one of four roles: owner, admin, member or viewer. Viewers can see links but cannot create or change them.

How many workspaces and members you can have depends on your plan.

## Plans

Free includes a monthly allowance of links and QR codes and a bio page. Paid plans raise the limits and add features such as custom keys, campaigns, analytics breakdowns and CSV export. Limits reset every billing period, and existing links keep redirecting on any plan. See [Pricing](/en/pricing) for the current plans, or [Upgrading plans](/docs/en/guides/billing/upgrading-plans) to change yours.

## Next steps

- [Creating QR codes](/docs/en/guides/qr-codes/creating-qr-codes)
- [Creating bio pages](/docs/en/guides/bio-pages/creating-bio-pages)

en/guides/links/creating-links.title: Creating links
en/guides/links/creating-links.markdown:
# Creating links

A short link sends visitors to a destination URL and counts each visit. This guide covers the new-link form, from the destination to the advanced redirect rules, and importing links in bulk.

## Create a link

1. Open **Links** in the sidebar and select **New link**. You can also paste a URL anywhere on the Links page outside a text field, or press C.
2. Enter the **Destination URL**. This is the only required field.
3. Fill in any optional fields described below.
4. Select **Create link**.

Shortn copies the new short link to your clipboard and opens its overview. Each link you create counts towards your plan's monthly link limit, shown under **Usage** in the sidebar.

## Title and key suggestions

When you paste a destination, Shortn looks up the page. Once the details arrive, select **Use page title** to fill in the **Title**, or **Use suggested key** to take a readable key. Your own edits are never overwritten. If the page can't be read, enter a title yourself or leave it empty.

## Custom key

The key is the part after the domain, for example `example` in `shortn.at/example`. Leave **Custom key** empty for a random key, or type your own using letters, digits, `-` and `_`. Custom keys depend on your plan; if yours doesn't include them, the form says which plan does.

If you later rename a key, the old key keeps redirecting to the same link.

## Title, description and tags

**Title** and **Description** help you find the link in lists and analytics. Visitors don't see them.

Under **Tags**, search for an existing tag or type a new one to create it. A link can carry up to 50 tags. Tags power the filters on the Links page, in the campaign builder and in the bio page link picker.

## Password

Under **Password**, set a password that visitors must enter before they reach the destination, plus an optional **Hint** shown on the password page. Password protection depends on your plan.

## Advanced options

Expand **Advanced options** for redirect rules. Each group shows a one-line summary of its current setting.

- **Schedule and expiry**: set **Available from (UTC)** and **Expires at (UTC)**, an **Approximate lifetime visit limit**, and a **Fallback URL when unavailable** for visitors who arrive outside that window. The visit limit includes QR scans and is approximate, because simultaneous visits can exceed it.
- **Country targeting**: send visitors from specific countries to other URLs. Use two-letter country codes; the first matching rule wins.
- **Device targeting**: route by operating system, device type, or both.
- **Weighted rotation**: split traffic between up to 10 destinations by relative weight. Returning visitors keep the same destination.
- **App links**: open an iOS or Android app, with a fallback to the web destination or the app store.
- **Redirect and query parameters**: forward incoming query parameters, use a permanent HTTP 301 redirect, and set fixed UTM values. See [UTM parameters](/docs/en/guides/links/utm-parameters).
- **Social preview**: set the title, description and image that link-preview bots show when the link is shared.

## Import links from a CSV file

To create many links at once, select **Import** on the Links page. Upload a UTF-8 CSV file with a header row, up to 50,000 rows, then map its columns, review the validation results and create the valid links. Imported links count towards your plan's monthly limit.

## After you create a link

The link's page has tabs for **Overview**, **Analytics**, **QR code**, **UTM variants** and **Edit**. From the **QR code** tab you can select **Create a QR code** to make a printable code that uses this link.

Changes you save on **Edit** apply from the next click.

## Next steps

- [Managing links](/docs/en/guides/links/managing-links)
- [UTM parameters](/docs/en/guides/links/utm-parameters)
- [Creating QR codes](/docs/en/guides/qr-codes/creating-qr-codes)

en/guides/links/managing-links.title: Managing links
en/guides/links/managing-links.markdown:
# Managing links

The Links page is built for large libraries. You can search and filter on the server, select links across pages and apply one change to all of them, archive links you no longer need in view, and restore deleted links within 30 days.

## Find links

Open **Links** in the sidebar. The list shows 25 links per page, with **Previous** and **Next** to move between pages. Use the filters above the list:

- **Search**: matches the key, destination or title.
- **Tag**: pick one or more tags. The tag list searches every tag in the workspace, so it works even with hundreds of tags.
- **Status**: show only links that are **Password-protected**, that **Shows safety page**, or that are **Disabled**.
- **Created**: limit the list to a recent period or a custom date range.
- **Sort by**: **Newest first**, **Oldest first** or **Most clicks**.

Filters are part of the page address, so you can bookmark or share a filtered view.

A **Destination error** flag on a row means weekly checks of that destination returned errors. The checks are informational; the link keeps redirecting.

## Edit a link

1. Select the link to open its overview.
2. Open the **Edit** tab.
3. Change the destination, key, title, description, tags, password or advanced options.
4. Select **Save changes**.

Changes apply from the next click. If you change the key, the old key keeps redirecting to the same link.

## Select links across pages

Tick the checkbox on each row you want, or use **Select this page**. Your selection stays as you move between pages and change filters, so you can build it from several searches. The selection bar shows how many links are selected and the maximum for one action. Use **Clear selection** to start again.

## Bulk actions

With links selected, choose an action. Each one opens its own page where you can review the selected links, filter that review, and confirm. Filters on the review page only change what you see; the action applies to the whole selection.

- **Edit tags**: choose an **Operation**, either **Add tags**, **Remove tags** or **Replace all tags**, pick the tags, then select **Apply tag changes**. **Remove all tags** clears every tag from the selection.
- **Move to campaign**: choose a **Destination campaign** and select **Move selected links**. Each link keeps its UTM source, medium, term and content. This needs a plan with campaigns.
- **Archive**: moves the links out of the active list. See below.
- **Delete selected**: moves the links to Trash.

Members can delete only the links they created. If your selection includes other people's links, the delete page tells you how many it can delete.

## Archive

Archiving tidies the active list without breaking anything. Archived links keep redirecting, and they stay in their QR codes, campaigns and bio pages. Their analytics remain.

To see them, select **Archived** above the list. Select links there and choose **Unarchive** to return them to the active list.

## Delete and restore

Deleting a link stops its short URL immediately, including on printed QR codes. For 30 days:

- the link stays in **Trash**, and you can restore it with its key, settings, campaigns and bio page references;
- its key stays reserved, so nobody else can take it.

After 30 days the link is permanently removed. Aggregate analytics remain.

To restore links:

1. Select **Trash** above the list. The **Restore until** column shows each link's deadline.
2. Select the links you want, across pages if needed.
3. Select **Restore selected**.

In Trash and Archived you can also choose **Group this page** and **By first tag** to group the current page by tag.

## Export

Select **Export** on the Links page to prepare a file of every link that matches your current filters, across all pages. A CSV export can be imported back into Shortn later.

## Next steps

- [UTM parameters](/docs/en/guides/links/utm-parameters)
- [Organizing campaigns](/docs/en/guides/campaigns/organizing-campaigns)
- [Understanding analytics](/docs/en/guides/analytics/understanding-analytics)
